In the lightbox, a photo held by a record of a resource the user may read has an info button, which shows that record's details, as does the `i` key: in a sidebar beside the photo, or on a mobile screen in a sheet over the lower part of the screen, which Escape, its close button or a swipe down on its header closes. The details start closed, and the browser remembers whether they were left open for the next photo and gallery. They are the fields its record page's sections show, less its file and the field pointing at the record, as a table of labels and values, as the record API answers the user, so the server decides what they see, and a link to its record page. A user who may not read that resource sees the photo alone, without the info button, as everyone does when it has no other field to show. In `/api/meta`, a user who cannot read `image` gets the gallery without it, and one who cannot list the photos without them; a gallery left with neither is left out. The server checks when it starts that `image` is a file field and that `photos` fits the resources.

### Maps

`l.map(title, { latitude, longitude })` draws a map centred on a pin at the record's position, read from two number fields (`integer`, `bigint` or `decimal`) in decimal degrees, WGS84, at `zoom` (default 15, from 0 to 22). It pans and zooms with two fingers on a phone, and with Ctrl or Cmd and the wheel elsewhere, so the page scrolls past it.

```ts
.layout((r) => [
  l.map('Location', { latitude: r.latitude, longitude: r.longitude }),
  l.section('Coordinates', [r.latitude, r.longitude]),
])
```

The map is drawn with [MapLibre](https://maplibre.org) from the style the server names: `createAdmin`'s `options.maps.style`, else `PROTOBASE_MAP_STYLE_URL`, an http(s) URL of a MapLibre style. The style's sources may be [PMTiles](https://docs.protomaps.com/pmtiles/) archives (`pmtiles://https://...`), so the tiles can be one file on a bucket of your own. The tiles, sprites and fonts are fetched by the browser, so their host must answer the app's origins with CORS, and an archive with range requests. Without a style there is no map, nor is there one for a record whose fields hold no position or for a user who may not read them. MapLibre loads with the first map drawn, so a page without one does not load it.

A map display takes two number fields that are `.filterable()`, since it asks for the records inside its view with a filter on them, and the server refuses to start otherwise; an index on them, such as `(latitude, longitude)`, lets Postgres find those records. The filter and search of the list narrow what it shows. Where it looks is in the address, `/listings?display=map&map=52.37,4.89,12` (latitude, longitude, zoom), so Back, a reload or a shared link opens the same view; without one it fits every matching record. When none is in view, **Show all** fits them again.

#### Approximate positions

Some records know their position only roughly, such as a listing that gives its street but not its number. A map display marks those positions by a boolean field: `approximate`, true for an approximate position, or `exact`, false for one. Their markers are hollow with a dashed edge, a marker's label to a screen reader says the position is approximate, and the chosen record's card says **Approximate position**. Without the field, or where it holds neither, a position is exact.

Around an approximate position the map draws the area the record states: the GeoJSON `Polygon`, `MultiPolygon`, `LineString` or `MultiLineString` its `area` field holds, as a `json` field or the text of one, a geometry or a feature of one, such as a block or the street; else a circle of its `radius` field, a number of metres; else a circle of `defaultRadius` metres when the display names one. A record that states none of them on a display without a default has only its hollow marker, so the map shows no more than the data says. An area is drawn faintly in the markers' colour, a line as a wide stroke, and the chosen record's darker. It fades in as the map zooms close enough for it to be wider than a marker, and only the records in view have theirs drawn.

```ts
d.map(
  { latitude: r.latitude, longitude: r.longitude, exact: r.coordinates_exact, radius: r.accuracy_m, area: r.street_outline },
  { label: 'Map', defaultRadius: 250 },
)
```

`radius`, `area` and `defaultRadius` need `approximate` or `exact`, and the server refuses to start when a field is of another type. A user who may not read the field that marks the positions sees them as exact.

A map does not edit the position: list the fields in a section as well when users should change them. The [property portal example](https://github.com/PrototeamHQ/protobase/tree/main/examples/property-portal) shows a listing on a map, and its listings on one.

#### Map layers

`options.maps.layers` adds other maps of raster tiles, such as aerial photos, next to the style. With layers, every map (`l.map` and `d.map`) has a switch in its top left corner between **Map**, the style's map and the default, and each layer by its `label`. The choice is remembered in the browser for every map, and a layer the app no longer offers falls back to the default. The chosen layer is drawn over the style's map, under the areas and markers, and its `attribution` shows in the map's corner while it is.

```ts
createAdmin({
  // ...
  options: {
    maps: {
      layers: [
        {
          id: 'aerial_nl',
          label: 'Aerial (NL)',
          tiles: 'https://service.pdok.nl/hwh/luchtfotorgb/wmts/v1_0/Actueel_orthoHR/EPSG:3857/{z}/{x}/{y}.jpeg',
          attribution: 'Luchtfoto <a href="https://www.beeldmateriaal.nl/">Beeldmateriaal Nederland</a>, CC BY 4.0, via <a href="https://www.pdok.nl/">PDOK</a>',
          bounds: [3.2, 50.7, 7.3, 53.7],
          maxzoom: 21,
        },
      ],
    },
  },
})
```

| Field | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | Lowercase letters, digits and `_`, unique: what the browser remembers. |
| `label` | What the switch says. |
| `tiles` | The http(s) URL of 256-pixel Web Mercator tiles with `{z}`, `{x}` and `{y}`: an XYZ service, or a WMTS `GetTile` URL in its `GoogleMapsCompatible` or `EPSG:3857` tile matrix set, with `{z}` as the tile matrix, `{y}` the row and `{x}` the column. |
| `attribution` | The credit the tiles' licence asks for; it may hold links. |
| `bounds` | Optional `[west, south, east, north]` in degrees, where the tiles are. The layer is offered everywhere; outside its bounds no tiles are asked for and the style's map shows through. |
| `maxzoom` | Optional deepest zoom of the tiles, from 0 to 24 (default 22); closer in, the map enlarges them. |

The browser fetches the tiles, so their host must answer the app's origins with CORS. Layers need a style: without one there is no map to switch. A layer that is not as above stops the server at startup. Use only tiles whose terms allow it: open aerial photos are published per country, such as the Netherlands' [PDOK Luchtfoto](https://www.pdok.nl/-/open-data-hr-luchtfoto) and Spain's [PNOA](https://pnoa.ign.es/) from the IGN, both CC BY 4.0, free and without a key; the [property portal example](https://github.com/PrototeamHQ/protobase/tree/main/examples/property-portal) offers both.

### Related records

Without any configuration, the record page's rail has a **Related records** card that counts the records pointing at this one: per resource, and per relation when one resource has two, such as Orders (Customer) and Orders (Supplier), how many there are, linking to its list filtered on this record (`/orders?filter=customer_id = "7"`). It counts each filterable relation to a resource with a one-field key, so an index serves the count, and leaves out a resource's tenant, a resource the user cannot list or whose relation they cannot read, the lines drawn on the page, and a relation an `l.related` section of the page already lists.

`l.related(title, options)` lists the first records of `resource` that point at the record on the page, in the table or display the resource's list page uses (with its switch, and on a phone its cards in one sideways row, as a [`Table` block](blocks.md#table)) shows them), and links to all of them in that list. They point at it directly, through a relation field, or through a join resource (`through`), such as the leases a tenant signed through `lease_tenants`:

| Option | |
| --- | --- |
| `resource` | The records listed. Required. |
| `field` | Without `through` or `from`: the relation on `resource` that holds this record's key. With `from`: the field of `resource` that holds that value. With `through`: the field of `resource` matched against the keys the join records hold. Filterable. Required. |
| `from` | A field of this record whose value `field` must hold, instead of this record's key, such as the task of a question, to list the task's links: `{ resource: 'task_links', field: 'task_id', from: 'task_id' }`. Same type as `field` (a relation to the same resource), not sensitive, and not with `through`. A record with no value lists nothing. |
| `through` | `{ resource, field, key?, filter? }`: the join records whose `field` (a filterable relation) holds this record's key; their `key` values (default their primary key) pick the listed records. All of them are read. |
| `filter`, `sort` | AIP-160 and AIP-132 on `resource`, as in the list API. `filter` narrows the listed records, `through.filter` the join records. |
| `columns` | Fields of `resource`, through relations too (`unit_id.property_id`); default the view's list columns without `field`. The first links to the record a row opens. |
| `open` | The relation of `resource` whose record a row opens, for rows that link this record to another. By default the one relation in `resource`'s primary key besides `field`, when there is exactly one (a join resource such as `task_dependencies` keyed on `[task_id, type, depends_on_id]`); otherwise rows open their own records. The row's menu then has **Open** for the other record and **Edit** for the link itself. |
| `limit` | How many records it shows, 1 to 100; default 10. When there are more, the section says so beside View all, such as "The first 10 of 37.". Before 0.13 this was `pageSize`, rows per page; rename it. |
| `display` | The display of `resource`'s list it opens in, such as `cards`; default the list's. |
| `help`, `empty` | A line under the title, and the text when nothing matches (default "Nothing here yet."). |
| `hideEmpty` | `true` leaves the section off the page while it has no records. |

The real estate example lists who a unit is let to (the primary tenant and co-signers of the lease that runs today) and that lease:

```ts title="examples/real-estate/config/units/ui.ts"
import { l, view } from '@protobase/schema'
import type { units } from './data'

/** A lease that covers today; `end_date` is its last day. */
const running = 'start_date <= now() AND (isNull(end_date) OR end_date >= now())'

export const unitsView = view<typeof units>('units')
  .title((r) => r.label)
  .names({ singular: 'Unit', plural: 'Units' })
  .nav({ recent: { status: 'status', tones: { vacant: 'warning', renovation: 'info' }, filter: 'status != "let"' } })
  .fields((r) => ({
    property_id: r.property_id.label('Property'),
    area_m2: r.area_m2.label('Area').help('Living area in m².').suffix(' m²'),
    energy_label: r.energy_label.format('badge'),
    base_rent: r.base_rent.label('Market rent').help('What a new lease would ask today, per month.').prefix('€').decimals(2),
    status: r.status.help('Let while a lease runs; vacant or under renovation between leases.').format('badge').valueLabels({ let: 'Let', vacant: 'Vacant', renovation: 'Renovation' }),
  }))
  .list((r) => ({ columns: [r.label, r.property_id, r.status, r.bedrooms, r.area_m2, r.energy_label, r.base_rent], search: [r.label] }))
  .filters((r, w) => [w.facets(r.status), w.facets(r.energy_label), w.range(r.base_rent, { histogram: true })])
  .layout((r) => [
    l.section('Unit', [r.property_id, r.label, r.floor, r.bedrooms, r.area_m2, r.energy_label]),
    l.section('Letting', [r.status, r.base_rent]),
    l.related('Let to', {
      resource: 'lease_tenants',
      field: 'lease_id',
      through: { resource: 'leases', field: 'unit_id', filter: running },
      // `primary` sorts after `co_signer`, so the primary tenant comes first
      sort: 'role desc',
      columns: ['tenant_id', 'role', 'tenant_id.email', 'tenant_id.phone'],
      help: 'The primary tenant and co-signers of the running lease.',
      empty: 'Vacant: no lease runs today.',
    }),
    l.related('Running lease', {
      resource: 'leases',
      field: 'unit_id',
      filter: running,
      columns: ['number', 'term', 'start_date', 'end_date', 'monthly_rent', 'service_costs'],
      empty: 'Vacant: no lease runs today.',
    }),
    l.sidebar([r.status, r.base_rent]),
  ])
```

When `resource` is ordered by hand within the record on the page (`.position(..., { within })` names `field`), the section has a **Reorder** button that puts its records in order by dragging them; see [Reordering by hand](#reordering-by-hand).

Every name is checked when the config loads. In `/meta` a caller who cannot read a resource the section names, or a field its filter or sort uses, does not get the section, and columns they cannot read are left out; the rows come from the list API with the caller's token, so row filters apply as everywhere else.

## Actions and views per role

```ts title="docs-examples/bike-shop/step-5.ts"
import { l } from '@protobase/schema'
import { customersView, repairsView as laidOut } from './step-4'

// Step 5: buttons for the moves the shop makes all day, and a quieter view for the mechanics.

export { customersView }

export const repairsView = laidOut.actions((a) => [
  a.update('ready', { label: 'Ready for pickup', icon: 'send', set: { status: 'ready' } }),
  a.update('collect', { label: 'Collected and paid', icon: 'wallet', set: { status: 'collected', paid: true }, confirm: 'Has the customer paid and taken the bike?' }),
  a.link('customerRepairs', { label: 'Other repairs of this customer', icon: 'file-text', to: { kind: 'list', resource: 'repairs', filter: 'customer_id = {customer_id}' } }),
])

/** What mechanics get instead: no money, and their own move. */
export const workshopRepairsView = laidOut
  .forRoles(['mechanic'])
  .list((r) => ({ columns: [r.number, r.bike, r.problem, r.status, r.mechanic], sort: [[r.booked_on, 'asc']], search: [r.number, r.bike] }))
  .filters((r, w) => [w.facets(r.status), w.facets(r.mechanic, { search: true }), w.dateRange(r.booked_on, { presets: ['7d', '30d', 'month'] })])
  .layout((r) => [l.section('The bike', [r.bike, r.problem]), l.section('In the workshop', [r.status, r.mechanic, r.notes]), l.sidebar([r.status, r.booked_on])])
  .actions((a) => [a.update('ready', { label: 'Ready for pickup', icon: 'send', set: { status: 'ready' } })])
```

`.actions((a) => [...])` names the moves a record page offers in its action rail, between **Edit**, when the record opens as a read view or locked, and **Delete**, for a user who may delete it, unless an `a.remove` deletes already; composed pages can put the same actions on buttons. On the form, **Save** leads the sidebar, above the rail, with **Cancel** under it when Edit opened the form; on a mobile screen they sit in a bar under the form instead. On a mobile screen, below `md` (768px), the rail's actions, Edit and Delete among them, sit in the top bar's **Record actions** menu (the ⋮ button), at hand however long the record is. `a.update`, `a.remove`, `a.link` and [`a.ai`](ai.md#ai-actions)), which has the model write a field, work without code; `a.action` runs a handler the app registers; it and `a.update` ask for their [inputs](#actions-that-ask-for-input) first when they have some. They are described with [named actions](layouts.md#named-actions)).

`.forRoles([...])` makes a view for users with one of those roles: each user gets the first such view that matches their roles, and the view without roles otherwise. A per-role view is a whole view, so build it from another (`laidOut.forRoles(...)` above) and change what differs.

The ERP's orders view uses most of this page at once, with a recent-record group in the sidebar:

```ts title="examples/erp/config/orders/ui.ts"
import { view } from '@protobase/schema'
import type { orders } from './data'

export const ordersView = view<typeof orders>('orders')
  .title((r) => r.number)
  .names({ singular: 'Order', plural: 'Orders' })
  .nav({
    recent: {
      status: 'status',
      tones: { draft: 'neutral', confirmed: 'info', picking: 'warning', shipped: 'success' },
      pulse: ['picking'],
      filter: 'status != "delivered" AND status != "cancelled"',
      orderBy: 'created_at desc',
    },
  })
  .fields((r) => ({
    status: r.status.help('Where the order is in its life. Moving it forward can notify the customer.').format('badge')
      .valueLabels({ draft: 'Draft', confirmed: 'Confirmed', picking: 'Picking', shipped: 'Shipped', delivered: 'Delivered', cancelled: 'Cancelled' }),
    total: r.total.help('Order total including VAT.').prefix('€').decimals(2),
    discount_percent: r.discount_percent.label('Discount').help('Percentage taken off the order total.').format('percent'),
    paid: r.paid.help('Set when the payment has been received.'),
    created_at: r.created_at.label('Created').format('absolute'),
  }))
  .list((r) => ({
    columns: [r.number, r.company_id, r.status, r.total, r.discount_percent, r.paid, r.owner_id, r.created_at],
    sort: [[r.created_at, 'desc']],
    search: [r.number],
  }))
  .filters((r, w) => [
    w.facets(r.status),
    w.facets(r.owner_id),
    w.dateRange(r.created_at, { presets: ['7d', '30d', '90d', 'quarter', 'year'] }),
    w.range(r.total, { histogram: true }),
    w.toggle(r.paid),
  ])
  .chart((r) => ({ field: r.created_at, range: '30d', granularity: 'day' }))
  .saveFeedback('toast')
  .actions((a) => [
    a.update('markPaid', { label: 'Mark as paid', icon: 'wallet', set: { paid: true }, confirm: 'Record that the customer paid this order?' }),
    a.action('createInvoice', { label: 'Create invoice', icon: 'file-text' }),
  ])
```

### Actions that ask for input

`inputs` on an `a.action` or an `a.update` makes its button open a dialog that asks for them first, each edited as the create form edits a field, with the action's `confirm` text above them and its label on the button that runs it. An `a.action`'s handler gets the answers as `values`, by input name:

```ts
.actions((a) => [
  a.action('remind', {
    label: 'Send reminder',
    icon: 'mail',
    inputs: (i) => [
      i.choice('channel', { label: 'Send by', options: [{ value: 'email', label: 'Email' }, { value: 'letter', label: 'Letter' }], default: 'email' }),
      i.text('note', { label: 'Note', multiline: true, optional: true, when: "channel = 'email'" }),
    ],
  }),
])
```

An `a.update` writes the answers with no code: a `set` value that is exactly `'{name}'` is the answer of the input called `name`. An empty answer writes `null`, an input that is hidden by `when` leaves its field as it is, and a `'{name}'` that names no input stops the config from loading. An update that asks for input is always offered, since the answer can always change the record. This button works the same on a composed page, so a dashboard can answer in place:

```ts
a.update('answer', { label: 'Answer', inputs: (i) => [i.text('answer', { label: 'Answer', multiline: true })], set: { answer: '{answer}' } })
```

| Input | Asks for |
| --- | --- |
| `i.text(name, o)` | A line of text, or several with `multiline: true`; `max` is the most characters it may have. |
| `i.integer(name, o)` | A whole number, which the handler gets as a number. |
| `i.decimal(name, o)` | A number with decimals, which the handler gets as text, as the API gives decimals, so no digit is lost. |
| `i.boolean(name, o)` | A switch, `true` or `false`, so it is never required. |
| `i.date(name, o)` | A date, `YYYY-MM-DD`. |
| `i.choice(name, { options })` | One of `options`, each a `value` with the `label` it reads as. |
| `i.choice(name, { resource })` | A record of `resource`, picked as the create form picks a relation; the handler gets its key. |
| `i.custom(name, { component, props? })` | What a [component](custom-components.md)) of the app's `protobase.ui.tsx`, by the name it is registered under, edits. |

Each takes `label`, and optionally `help`, a `default`, `optional: true` to allow an empty answer (every other input is required) and `when`, an AIP-160 condition over the inputs before it, as [`<Show when>`](layouts.md#conditions)) is over a record: `"start = 'github' OR code = 'github'"`. An input whose condition does not hold is hidden, not required and left out of `values`, and the inputs after it read it as empty. A `when` that names no input before it, a `default` that is not one of the options and a name given twice stop the config from loading; so does a choice of a resource the app does not have, when the server starts.

An empty answer is `null`. Before the handler runs, the dialog refuses a required answer left empty, a number that is none, a date that is not `YYYY-MM-DD` and a text longer than `max`, each under its input. When the handler throws an `ActionInputError` from `@protobase/ui`, such as `new ActionInputError({ email: 'No user has this address' })`, or an API error, such as a [function's](../guides/api-functions.md)) answer, whose errors name an input as their `field`, each message shows under its input and the dialog stays open; another error shows above the inputs. When it resolves, the dialog closes and the action ends as any other: everything shown of the resource reloads and a toast says it is done.

A custom input's component gets the answer as `value` (`null` when empty), `onChange`, `invalid` while its answer is refused, the input's `props` and the `input` itself (`ActionInputProps`), as a [field type's](custom-components.md#field-types)) editor does. Without that component the button is disabled, with the reason as its tooltip. In `/api/meta`, a user who cannot read the resource of a choice does not get the action.
